IMT towards 2030 and beyond (IMT-2030)

Page Content 10

​ITU-R WP 5D completed the work on the planned 3 draft Reports and confirmed date and location for the IMT-2030 Workshop (October 2026) New!​​​

​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

​

​

The work on the third report, addressing “Requirements, evaluation criteria and submission templates for the development of IMT-2030" **, was concluded, which provides the basis for the forthcoming evaluation of potential candidates for the terrestrial radio interface technology (RIT) for IMT-2030. More details on this document, the previous reports as well as the overall IMT-process, will be addressed at the IMT-2030 Workshop, which date and location has been confirmed: 12. February 2027, Geneva (October 2026) New!

** Note: This draft new Report has been submitted to the parent ITU-R Study Group 5 (SG 5) for approval in December 2026 (Document 5/126). Following approval, the Report will serve as the principal reference for the evaluation of candidate IMT-2030 RITs/SRITs within the IMT-2030 technology development process.


​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​ITU-R WP 5D completed the development of “Guidelines for evaluation of radio interface technologies for IMT-2030” (June 2026)​ ​​​

​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

At its June 2026 meeting, ITU-R WP 5D completed the draft new Report "Guidelines for evaluation of radio interface technologies for IMT-2030" **

This draft Report provides the framework for evaluating candidate IMT-2030 radio interface technologies (RITs/SRITs) against those requirements. It:​​

  • ​​Defines three evaluation methods — simulation, analytical, and inspection — with the applicable method pre-assigned for each technical performance criterion
  • Specifies seven test environments, including three newly introduced environments (Indoor Factory-HRLLC, Indoor Factory-ISAC, and Urban Macro-ISAC) not present in the IMT-2020 evaluation framework​​​​

    ​​​An according PDF-file can be found​ here​.

  • ​​Introduces extended channel models, including near-field, spatial non-stationarity, and ISAC-specific models, to support IMT-2030's sensing capabilities​
​** Note: This draft new Report has been submitted to the parent ITU-R Study Group 5 (SG 5) for approval in December 2026 (Document 5/119). Following approval, the Report will serve as the principal reference for the evaluation of candidate IMT-2030 RITs/SRITs within the IMT-2030 technology development process.
​

​​​​​​​​​ITU-R WP 5D completed the development of “IMT-2030 technical performance requirements” (February 2026)​ New!​​​

​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​



At its February 2026 meeting, ITU-R WP 5D has completed the draft new Report “Minimum requirements related to technical performance for IMT-2030 radio interface(s)” *​

As defined in Recommendation ITU-R M.2160, IMT-2030 is expected to provide enhanced and new capabilities beyond IMT-2020, guided by overarching design principles including: 

  • ​​​​Security and resilience​​
  • ​Connecting the unconnected
  • Ubiquitous intelligence
  • Sustainability​​
​IMT-2030 supports six usage scenarios:
IC (immersive communication), HRLLC (hyper reliable and low latency communication), MC (massive communication), UC (ubiquitous connectivity), AIAC (artificial intelligence and communication), and ISAC (integrated sensing and communication). ​​​

This draft Report addresses: 

  • Defines 20 minimum technical performance requirements​​​​​
  • Provides a consistent basis for specification and evaluation​​​
  • Supports the further development of the “Guidelines for evaluation of radio interface technologies for IMT‑2030” Report ITU-R M.[IMT-2030.EVAL] and further related deliverables​
  • Reflects ongoing global research and technology activities​​​
These requirements establish minimum performance levels for consideration by ITU-R, they do not restrict implementation approaches nor represent guaranteed real-world deployment performance.​
​
* Note: This draft new Report has been submitted to the parent ITU-R Study Group 5 (SG 5) for approval in 12/2026 (document 5/116). Furthermore, i​t is expected that WP 5D will conclude its work on the draft new Reports ITU-R M.[IMT-2030.EVAL] and ITU-R M.[IMT-2030.SUBMISSION] at its next meeting(s) and then those Reports ​​will be submitted to SG 5 as well.
​
​An according PDF-file can be found​ here​.​

​​​​​​​ITU agreed on Circular Letter (CL) inviting for candidate RIT for IMT-2030 ​​​

​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​At meeting #47 (10/24), WP 5D agreed on the CL to invite candidate radio interface technologies (RIT) for the terrestrial component of IMT-2030, which has been published as 5/LCCE/115​. This CL provides some background information on IMT-2030 (6G) and invites submissions of proposals for RIT-candidates for IMT-2030 to be received by ITU in the timeframe 02/2027-02/2029. As it was done for previous IMT-generations, ITU-R also informed “External Organisations” (i.e., Standardisation and Industry fora) about this CL. Meanwhile, ITU-R will continue the development of technical performance requirements (TPR) and common evaluation criteria. More information about the evaluation process and the related independent evaluation groups (IEG) is available on the new “Web page for the IMT-2030 submission and evaluation process”.

New Report ITU-R M.2541 “Technical feasibility of IMT in bands above 100 GHz” has been published (May 2024)

​​​​​​​​
At its first meeting in 2024, ITU-R SG 5 approved a new Report ITU-R M.2541 about the “Technical feasibility of IMT in bands above 100 GHz”, which includes information on propagation mechanisms and channel models, as well as newly developed technology enablers su​ch as active and passive components, antenna techniques, deployment architectures, and the results of simulations and performance tests. As such, it complements Report ITU-R M.2376 containing studies for the frequency ranges 6-100 GHz.

New Recommendation ITU-R M.2160 on the “IMT-2030 Framework” (November 2023)

Page Content 2

​​​​​The Radiocommunication Assembly 2023 (RA-23) approved the revisions of Resolution ITU-R 56, confirming the name for the next generation of IMT (aka “6G”) to be “IMT-2030” and Resolution ITU-R 65, which describes the principles of the IMT-process. Along these revisions, RA-23 also approved the new Recommendation on the “IMT-2030 Framework”, which will now become Recommendation ITU-R M. 2160.
​​

Together with the already existing Report on “Future Technology Trends” ITU-R M.2516 (see below), this marks the achievement of the initial phase, setting the basis for the development of IMT-2030. The next phase (2024-2027) will be the definition of relevant requirements and evaluation criteria for potential radio interface technologies (RIT) for IMT-2030 – (see “ITU-R timeline for IMT-2030” below).

With the evolution of information and communications technologies, IMT-2030 is expected to support enriched and potential immersive experience, enhanced ubiquitous coverage, and enable new forms of collaboration. Furthermore, IMT-2030 is envisaged to support expanded and new usage scenarios compared to those of IMT-2020, while providing enhanced and new capabilities.​

IMT-2030 is further expected to help address the need for increased environmental, social, and economic sustainability, and also support the goals of the Paris Agreement of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change.​

Perspective on the “ITU-R Framework for IMT-2030” (July 2023 / October 2024)

​​​​​​​​


​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​ITU-R WP 5D provides a ​​perspective on the “ITU-R Framework for IMT-2030” (updated October 2024 - PDF see ​here).​​

To promote collaboration on the overall development of IMT-2030, this perspective has been shared at the ITU-T Workshop on "Future technology trends towards 2030“​ (24./25. July 2023).​​​​

ITU-R WP 5D agrees on “IMT-2030 Framework” (June 2023)​

​​​​​​​​At its June 2023 meeting, ITU-R WP 5D has agreed the draft new Recommendation “Framework and overall objectives of the future development ​of IMT for 2030 and beyond”*​​, which can be considered as the basis for the standardisation fora to develop the next generation of​ IMT standards​​.

​This draft Recommendation addresses: 
  • ​​Trends of IMT-2030 ​​​
  • Usage scenarios of IMT-2030 
  • Capabilities of IMT-2030 ​
  • Considerations of ongoing development ​​

ITU-R Report on “Future Technology Trends” (December 2022)

Page Content 3
ITU-R WP 5D developed a new ITU-R Report on “Future Technology Trends”, which has been published as Report
​ITU-R M.2516​ in December 2022. This Report provides a broad view of future technical aspects of terrestrial IMT systems considering the timeframe up to 2030 and beyond, characterized with respect to key emerging services, applications trends and relevant driving factors and is applicable to radio interfaces, mobile terminals, and radio access networks by considering the timeframe up to 2030 and beyond.





​​​​

ITU-R Working Party 5D agrees on the overview timeline for IMT towards the year 2030 and beyond (June 2022)

Page Content 4
​​​​​​​​​​The work and discussion on a new timeline started in WP 5D #37 and during its meeting #41 (June 2022), ITU-R WP 5D agreed on the overview timeline for IMT towards the year 2030 and beyond. ​
The agreement is described in detail in Attachment 2.12 to Chapter 2 of Document 5D/1361 (Meeting report WP 5D #41) and describes the process and shows the anticipated deliverables for the development of IMT towards 2030 and beyond. It has been agreed that the well-known process and deliverable formats utilized for IMT-2000, IMT-Advanced, and IMT-2020 should be utilized also for IMT towards 2030 and beyond and considered as a “model” for the IMT deliverables to leverage on the prior work.​

​














An according PDF-file can be found here​.

Workshop on “IMT for 2030 and beyond” (14th June 2022)

Page Content 5

ITU-R WP 5D held a full-day Workshop on “IMT for 2030 and beyond”, with total 348 participants in an integrated physical and remote participants arrangement. The objective of the Workshop was to provide WP 5D delegates with an overview of ongoing worldwide research activities, initiatives, and views related to future mobile communications targeting 2030 and beyond (details see here). ​

Fourteen presentations were made from various ITU-R members, external organizations, research projects and academia and in reflecting on the presentations, the following graphic considers keyword theme from each presentation organized within the context of the currently planned sections of the WP 5D working document towards a preliminary draft new Recommendation ITU-R M.[IMT.VISION 2030 AND Beyond]:

On the road to “IMT towards 2030 and beyond” (February 2022)
ITU-R WP 5D has started the work on “IMT towards 2030 and beyond” by applying the well-proven IMT-process, which has already been implemented for IMT-2000, IMT-Advanced and IMT-2020, resulting in Recommendations ITU-R M.1457, M.2012 and M.2150 respectively.  
As one of the targets at the beginning of the process, ITU-R WP 5D developed a new ITU-R Report on “Future Technology Trends”. ​At the meeting of the parent ITU-R SG 5​ in November 2022, this document has been agreed and was published as Report ITU-R M.2​516.

The next documents ​developed within ITU-R are:  
  • ITU-R Recommendation on a new “IMT-2030 Framework” (in former generations named “IMT-Vision”)​ … meanwhile available as Rec. ITU-R M.2160
  • ITU-R Report on “Technical feasibility of IMT in bands above 100 GHz”​​​ … meanwhile available as Rep. ITU-R M.2541

Page Content 11

​​IMT-2030 is expected to provide enhanced capabilities compared to those described for IMT-2020 in Recommendation ITU-R M.2083, as well as new capabilities to support the expanded usage scenarios of IMT-2030.​

Enhanced capabilities for IMT-2030​​

  • Peak Data Rate: Ideal maximum data rate per device, exceeding IMT-2020; targets include 50–200 Gbps depending on specific scenarios.
  • User Experienced Data Rate: Data rates ubiquitously available; targets include 300–500 Mbps or higher, adaptable to various conditions.
  • Spectrum Efficiency: Average data throughput per unit spectrum; aimed to be 1.5–3 times better than IMT-2020.
  • Area Traffic Capacity: Total throughput per area; targets include 30–50 Mbps/m² or more.

  • Connection Density: Devices connected per km²; targets range from 106 – 108 devices/km². 

  • Mobility: Seamless connectivity at speeds up to 500–1,000 km/h.

  • Latency: Radio network latency reduced to 0.1–1 ms.

  • Reliability: High reliability, ensuring successful data transmission with success probabilities of 1-10−5 to 1-10−7.

  • Security and Resilience: Enhanced protection against cyber threats and robust operation during disruptions.

New capabilities of IMT-2030
  • Coverage: Improved cell edge service range through enhanced link budgets.
  • Positioning: High-precision positioning with accuracy of 1–10 cm.
  • Sensing: Advanced capabilities like object detection, localization, imaging, mapping, etc.
  • AI Integration: AI-enabled features such as distributed learning, data processing, and AI model inference, etc.
  • Sustainability: Reduced environmental impact through energy-efficient systems and resource optimization.
  • Interoperability: Seamless functioning across diverse systems with transparent standards.​

​​※ These capabilities are based on Recommendation ITU-R M.2160-0 “Framework and overall objectives of the future development of IMT for 2030 and beyond“.
